summary: A single simple moving average line on the price chart: the plain average of the last 20 closes by default.
overview: The Simple Moving Average (SMA) draws one line that is the plain average of the last N values. By default it averages 20 closing prices and is drawn in blue.
You can change the source, shift the line with an offset, and pick its color.
how: SMA = sum of the last N values / N. Each bar in the window counts the same, and the oldest bar drops out when a new one arrives.
Because every bar weighs the same, the SMA is smoother but slower to react than an EMA of the same length.
use: Some traders watch whether price closes above or below the line.
Use its slope to read the direction of the trend.
Add a second SMA of another length and watch where they cross.
Some traders use well-known lengths like 50 or 200 as broad trend references.
alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
The line can jump when a large bar drops out of the window.
